capacity.capacity_definition: Equinix reports retail capacity in cabinet equivalents, not MW; no company-wide operational MW figure is disclosed (built_active_mw = null). Operating footprint per Q2 2026 materials: 282 IBX data centers across 77 markets in 36 countries (the FY2025 10-K said 280 across 77 markets/36 countries), 10,500+ customers, 230 cloud on-ramps, 522,700 total interconnections (record +9,700 net adds in Q2). Cabinet utilization ~78% overall as of June 30, 2026; stabilized data centers ~82% utilized; 4,200 net billed cabinets added in Q2; MRR per cabinet $2,538 (+6% y/y normalized/constant-currency). total_pipeline_mw = 3,000 MW: on the Q2 2026 call management said Equinix controls ~3 GW of land/developable capacity with ~700 MW under active construction across 52 major projects in 33 markets (new projects announced in Chicago, Istanbul and Johor in Q2). contracted_or_secured_power_mw = 3,000 MW per management's call statement that for the 3 GW it 'either has contracted power or a high degree of confidence that power will be contracted' — i.e., a mix of contracted and high-confidence, not fully contracted. contracted_unbuilt_mw = 182 MW is the pre-leased portion of the 196 MW of xScale (hyperscale JV) capacity under development; in Q2 alone Equinix closed 134 MW of xScale leases in the Americas (including the Hampton, GA transaction that generated ~$120M of non-recurring fees). 2025 analyst day 'Build Bolder' plan (June 25, 2025): double data center capacity by 2029 — building as much in five years as in the prior 27 — on ~3 GW of developable capacity, originally with $4-5B/yr capex; at Q2 2026 the long-term outlook was raised to $5-7B capex annually through 2029 (2026 capex now $5-6B). AI commentary: CEO Adaire Fox-Martin — 'The AI infrastructure cycle is accelerating, especially inference'; majority of large deals were AI-driven; demand strength cited in inference and sovereign AI workloads; ~7,000 cabinets being accelerated from 2027 into Q4 2026.

financials.revenue_basis: FY2026 guidance midpoints used as NTM proxy (calendar-2026 guidance, not a true next-twelve-months figure). Raised FY2026 guidance from the July 29, 2026 release: revenues $10.205-10.285B (+~11-12% y/y, as-reported and normalized/constant-currency); adjusted EBITDA $5.210-5.270B (~51% margin, ~+2pp expansion); AFFO $4.240-4.300B (+13-14% as-reported); AFFO per share $42.69-43.29 (+11-13% as-reported, 10-12% normalized/CC). Management called it 'the largest single guidance raise in the history of our company.' Q2 2026 actuals: revenue $2.625B (+16% y/y as-reported, +11% normalized/CC MRR basis), adjusted EBITDA $1.396B (53% margin, +300bps y/y), AFFO/share $11.78 (+20% as-reported per press release rendering; Zacks computes +18.9%), boosted by ~$120-124M of non-recurring xScale/JV fees (Hampton). Long-term outlook raised: 2027-2029 revenue growth 10-13%/yr and AFFO/share growth 9-12%/yr (vs. analyst-day 5-9% AFFO/share).
financials.backlog_definition: Remaining performance obligations (RPO) per the Q2 2026 Form 10-Q (eqix-20260630.htm): approximately $15.0B as of June 30, 2026 (figure via StockTitan/search renderings of the 10-Q; direct EDGAR fetch blocked by egress proxy). This is ASC 606 RPO — contracted future colocation/interconnection/services revenue not yet recognized — distinct from annualized bookings (Q2 annualized gross bookings $424M, +23%, second-highest ever).
financials.valuation_basis: Market cap / EV not extracted — not verifiable against primary sources in this session (equity market data sites blocked by egress proxy); left null rather than estimated.

companies.caveats: SOURCING: The sandbox egress proxy blocked ALL direct fetches (sec.gov, efts.sec.gov, newsroom.equinix.com, investor.equinix.com, prnewswire.com, stocktitan.net, cloudfront PDFs, transcript sites), so every figure was extracted from search-engine renderings of the primary documents (press release, 10-Q, call transcripts) and cross-checked across 2+ independent renderings where possible; quotes are verbatim as rendered by the search tool, not re-verified character-for-character against EDGAR. NET DEBT: $21,174M = total debt principal $22,153M minus cash & equivalents $979M (strict task definition). Including short-term investments (cash+STI $2.2B), net debt is ~$20.0B, which reconciles with the company-stated net leverage of 3.6x annualized adjusted EBITDA (3.6 x $1.396B x 4 = ~$20.1B). Gross debt ~$22B carries a ~3.0% blended after-tax rate and 6.4-year weighted average maturity; finance lease liabilities are excluded from the $22,153M principal figure. Total debt is above the $17-20B range suggested in the task brief — Equinix has been issuing to fund the Build Bolder capex ramp. CAPACITY: built/active MW is genuinely not disclosed (cabinet-based reporting); the 3 GW is a land-bank/developable figure, only ~700 MW of it under active construction, and power is 'contracted or high-confidence' rather than fully contracted. xScale MW largely sits in unconsolidated JVs (~2 GW program at full buildout, >$23B total investment; Equinix holds 20-25% equity stakes — 25% in the US GIC/CPPIB JV) and xScale revenue reaches Equinix mainly as fees/equity income, so JV MW is NOT on Equinix's balance sheet; the 134 MW Q2 leasing included ~$120M one-time Hampton fees that flattered Q2 revenue/AFFO growth (Americas +25% included $124M non-recurring JV services). MINOR DISCREPANCIES: data center count 282 (Q2 2026 rendering) vs 280 (FY2025 10-K); major projects 52 across 33 markets (Q2 call) vs 58 at the June 2025 analyst day; AFFO/share growth +20% (press release, as-reported) vs +18.9% (Zacks calc). RPO 'approximately $15.0B' came from a single-source rendering of the 10-Q (StockTitan) though repeated consistently across two separate searches. FY guidance figures are company guidance (calendar 2026), used as NTM proxies. One search result referenced a '$4B atNorth acquisition in Q1 2026' from a low-authority blog — unverified, excluded. Valuation/market cap deliberately left null (no reachable primary source).

capacity.capacity_definition: IT load MW (DLR's standard disclosure basis). built_active_mw = ~3.1 GW of in-service IT capacity across ~310 data centers ('approximately 3.1 gigawatts of IT capacity'), consolidated portfolio occupancy 89.8% at 6/30/26 (White Space IT Load basis, excludes capacity under active development/held for development; Americas 95.2%, EMEA 81.9%, APAC 85.9%; up from 89.3% at YE25; FY26 guidance for occupancy +75-125 bps). contracted_unbuilt_mw = 1.4 GW under construction at ~$20B total cost, 63% pre-leased (pro forma for hyperscale leases signed in July 2026) at an 11.5% average expected stabilized yield; pipeline doubled in 1H26 (Q2: delivered 76 MW ~60% pre-leased, started 312 MW). contracted_or_secured_power_mw = in-service 3.1 GW + 1.4 GW under active construction (powered/secured); excludes the Kansas City land buy (~$475M, up to 2 GW of utility power) closed in Q2. total_pipeline_mw = 3.1 GW in-service + ~8.5 GW of 'buildable IT capacity under active development and held for future development' (i.e., ~7.1 GW of land/shell held for future development beyond the 1.4 GW under construction). gpu_count: n/a - DLR is a landlord (wholesale/colo REIT), does not own GPUs.

financials.backlog_definition: Record backlog of signed-but-not-yet-commenced leases = $1.9B of ANNUALIZED GAAP base rent at 100% share at 6/30/26 ($1.4B at DLR's pro-rata share, +75% YTD, ~30% of in-place data center rent). Commencement cadence per call: ~$635M of annualized rent scheduled to commence in 2H26 and ~$480M in 2027, remainder thereafter. This is an annualized-rent figure, NOT total contract value - hyperscale leases run long (e.g., the 288 MW NoVA assets carry 15-year leases with 3.6% escalators), so cumulative contracted revenue is a large multiple of $1.9B. The 10-Q lessor schedule of total future minimum lease payments receivable (the biggest contracted-$ figure) could not be retrieved because the egress proxy blocks sec.gov/EDGAR; DLR discloses the full multi-year schedule in filings (10-K/10-Q) but no search-indexed rendering of the 6/30/26 total was found, so it is deliberately not estimated here. Q2'26 bookings: $307M annualized GAAP base rent at 100% share / $208M at DLR share, comprising $87.8M 0-1MW (42%), record $20.5M interconnection (10%, +18% YoY), and $99.8M >1MW (48%); 0-1MW + interconnection = record $108M, third straight quarterly record. Headline deal: 200 MW AI-inference hyperscale lease in Charlotte, the largest MW transaction in company history; renewals >$261M signed at cash re-leasing spreads above 25% (0-1MW +5.2% cash MTM; >1MW +66.7%).
financials.revenue_basis: FY2026 guidance midpoints as proxy for NTM (raised at Q2'26 print): total revenue $6,850-$6,950M excluding promote income (raised from $6,600-$6,700M); Adjusted EBITDA $3,750-$3,850M (raised from $3,600-$3,700M); Core FFO/sh ex-net-promote $8.15-$8.20 (from $8.00-$8.10); constant-currency Core FFO/sh ex-net-promote $8.10-$8.15; net capex guidance $4.25-$4.75B. Actual Q2'26: total revenue ~$1.9B (+18% QoQ, +29% YoY), Adjusted EBITDA $978M (+6% QoQ, +19% YoY), Core FFO/sh $2.65 reported incl. $0.52 of net promote ($188M net promote income from the Blackstone development JV), $2.13 ex-promote (+14% YoY vs $1.87).
financials.valuation_basis: Equity market capitalization ~$72.77B (stockanalysis.com, ~mid-Aug 2026; ~376.7M shares, ~$193/sh implied). Adding consolidated net debt (~$16.7B) and preferred implies EV ~$90B; company-reported debt-plus-preferred-to-total-enterprise-value was 22.3% at Q2'26. Net debt built as: total debt ~$18.6B at 6/30/26 ($17.0B unsecured + ~$1.6B secured/other) minus $1.86B cash = ~$16.74B consolidated. Company-defined net leverage (includes pro-rata share of unconsolidated JV debt and pro-rata EBITDA): net debt-to-Adjusted-EBITDA 4.7x at Q2'26 (down 0.4 turns over 12 months); fixed charge coverage 5.2x. Per-share JV debt at DLR share not separately retrievable from blocked supplemental, but the 4.7x on ~$3.9B annualized adj. EBITDA implies pro-rata net debt ~$18B+, i.e., roughly $1.5-2B of net JV-share debt on top of the consolidated figure.
